ordered_diagnoses: Orbital Apex Syndrome due to Streptococcus constellatus

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of headache and vision loss with sinus inflammation and orbital involvement
salient_findings: Severe headache with worsening over time
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
No history of chronic or allergic rhinosinusitis
Recent diagnosis of COVID-19
Developed rhinorrhea three weeks prior to presentation
Recovered from COVID-19 but developed worsening headache and vision loss
Right eye visual acuity limited to hand-motion detection
Severe pain on ocular motion
Sinus cultures positive for Streptococcus constellatus
Elevated Serum IgG4 level
Dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells with most being IgG4 positive

raw.rationale: Elevated Serum IgG4 level and dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells with most being IgG4 positive, which are characteristic findings of IgG4-related disease, along with the patient's clinical presentation of worsening headache and vision loss following a recent COVID-19 diagnosis.

rejected.label: Orbital Apex Syndrome due to Streptococcus constellatus
rejected.why: While sinus cultures were positive for Streptococcus constellatus, the presence of elevated IgG4 levels and IgG4-positive plasma cells suggests a primary inflammatory process rather than an infectious one.

rejected.label: Orbital Cellulitis
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and laboratory findings, particularly the elevated IgG4 levels and histopathological findings, do not support a diagnosis of orbital cellulitis, which is typically an infectious process.

rejected.label: Invasive Fungal Sinusitis
rejected.why: There is no mention of fungal elements in the histopathological examination or other evidence to support a diagnosis of invasive fungal sinusitis.

rejected.label: IgG4-related disease
rejected.why: While this is a broader category that includes IgG4-Related Orbital Disease, the specific involvement of the orbit and the clinical context make IgG4-Related Orbital Disease a more precise diagnosis for this case.
